sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第097卷

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 97.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀十九】　起玄黓攝提格，盡強圉協洽，凡六年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 19] Beginning Xuanji Shetige, ending Qiangyu Xiejia, six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 19] From Xuanji Shetige through Qiangyu Xiejia—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new-moon day jìwèi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (jìwèi), the day of the new moon, a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On yǐchǒu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On yǐchǒu the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史庾懌以酒餉江州刺史王允之；

translations.literal: Yu Yi, Inspector of Yuzhou, sent wine as a gift to Wang Yunzhi, Inspector of Jiangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, the inspector of Yuzhou, sent wine as a gift to Wang Yunzhi, the inspector of Jiangzhou;

sentences.zh: 允之覺其毒，飲犬，犬斃，密奏之。

translations.literal: Yunzhi detected that it was poisoned, gave it to a dog to drink, the dog died, and he secretly memorialized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhi detected poison in the wine, gave some to a dog, and when the dog died he secretly reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「大舅已亂天下，小舅復欲爾邪！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The elder maternal uncle has already thrown the realm into disorder—does the younger maternal uncle wish to do the same!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The elder uncle by marriage has already thrown the realm into chaos—does the younger uncle mean to do the same!"

sentences.zh: 」二月，懌飲鴆而卒。

translations.literal: " In the second month, Yi drank poisoned wine and died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the second month Yi was made to drink poisoned wine and died.

sentences.zh: 三月，初以武悼-{后}-配食武帝廟。

translations.literal: In the third month, for the first time Empress Wuzhao was paired for sacrifice in Emperor Wu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the court for the first time paired Empress Wuzhao for joint sacrifice in Emperor Wu's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 庾翼在武昌，數有妖怪，欲移鎮樂鄉。

translations.literal: Yu Yi was at Wuchang; strange omens occurred repeatedly, and he wished to move his headquarters to Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu Yi held Wuchang, strange omens kept appearing, and he wished to move his command post to Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 征虜長史王述與庾冰箋曰：「樂鄉去武昌千有餘里，數萬之眾，一旦移徙，興立城壁，公私勞擾。

translations.literal: Wang Shu, chief clerk of the Campaign against the Barbarians, wrote to Yu Bing: "Lexiang is more than a thousand li from Wuchang; tens of thousands of men, if moved all at once to raise walls and build a city, will weary both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, chief clerk on Yu Yi's staff, wrote to Yu Bing: "Lexiang lies more than a thousand li from Wuchang. To shift tens of thousands of men at a stroke, erect walls, and build a new city would exhaust both the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 又江州當溯流數千里，供給軍府，力役增倍。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiangzhou would have to go upstream several thousand li to supply the military headquarters, doubling corvée and transport burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou would also have to haul supplies upstream for thousands of li to feed the army headquarters, doubling labor and transport levies.

sentences.zh: 且武昌實江東鎮戍之中，非但扞御上流而已；

translations.literal: Moreover Wuchang truly stands at the center of Jiangdong's garrison line—not only to defend the upper Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang moreover stands at the very center of Jiangdong's defensive chain; its role is not merely to guard the upper Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 緩急赴告，駿奔不難。

translations.literal: in emergency, reports and swift relief are not hard to deliver.
translations.idiomatic: In an emergency, word can reach it and relief can arrive without great delay.

sentences.zh: 若移樂鄉，遠在西陲，一朝江渚有虞，不相接救。

translations.literal: If the seat is moved to Lexiang, far on the western fringe, once there is alarm along the river islets, rescue cannot connect.
translations.idiomatic: If the headquarters were moved to Lexiang on the far western marches, a sudden threat along the river could not be met in time.

sentences.zh: 方岳重將，固當居要害之地，為內外形勢，使窥窬之心不知所向。

translations.literal: A regional commander of the first rank ought to hold a strategic position, forming inner and outer posture so that covetous designs do not know where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: A commander of such rank should hold a strategic post that shapes the whole defensive posture inward and outward, so that would-be aggressors cannot tell where to strike.

sentences.zh: 昔秦忌亡胡之讖，卒為劉、項之資；

translations.literal: Formerly Qin dreaded the omen of "the barbarian who will destroy Hu," and in the end it became the capital of Liu and Xiang;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Qin dreaded the prophecy that "a barbarian will destroy Hu," yet that very fear in the end supplied the means for Liu Bang and Xiang Yu.

sentences.zh: 周圍惡檿弧之謠，而成褒姒之亂。

translations.literal: Zhou was beset by the song of the mulberry bow and the calamity of Baosi came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was consumed by dread of the mulberry-bow prophecy, and the disaster of Baosi followed.

sentences.zh: 是以達人君子，直道而行，禳避之道，皆所不取；

translations.literal: Therefore the enlightened gentleman walks the straight path and does not resort to rites of averting ill omens;
translations.idiomatic: For this reason a man of insight keeps to the straight course and rejects every rite meant to ward off ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 正當擇人事之勝理，思社稷之長計耳。

translations.literal: one should choose what is sound in human affairs and think of the long-term plan for the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: He should choose what human effort can best accomplish and plan for the lasting good of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」朝議亦以為然。

translations.literal: " Court opinion also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court discussion likewise endorsed this view.

sentences.zh: 翼乃止。

translations.literal: Yi then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，乙卯，帝不豫；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on yǐmǎo, the emperor fell gravely ill;

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅，疾篤。

translations.literal: in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his illness became critical.
translations.idiomatic: and in the sixth month, on gēngyín, his condition turned critical.

sentences.zh: 或詐為尚書符，敕宮門無得內宰相；

translations.literal: Someone forged an order in the name of the Secretariat forbidding the palace gates to admit the chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Someone forged a Secretariat order barring chief ministers from entering the palace gates;

sentences.zh: 眾皆失色。

translations.literal: all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: and everyone turned pale with alarm.

sentences.zh: 庾冰曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Yu Bing said, "This must be a fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing said, "This must be a forgery."

sentences.zh: 」推問，果然。

translations.literal: " On investigation, it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: " Investigation proved that it was.

sentences.zh: 帝二子丕、弈，皆在襁褓。

translations.literal: The emperor's two sons Pi and Yi were both still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's two sons, Pi and Yi, were both still infants.

sentences.zh: 庾冰自以兄弟秉權日久，恐易世之後，親屬愈疏，為它人所間，每說帝以國有強敵，宜立長君；

translations.literal: Yu Bing, considering that he and his brothers had held power long, feared that after a change of reign kinsmen would grow more distant and others would drive wedges between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful enemies abroad the state should install an elder sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing, knowing that he and his brothers had held power for years, feared that after a change of reign their kin would be pushed aside and others would come between them; he repeatedly urged the emperor that with powerful foes abroad the throne should pass to a mature heir.

sentences.zh: 請以母親弟琅邪王岳為嗣，帝許之。

translations.literal: he asked that the emperor's younger maternal half-brother, Prince of Langye Yue, be made heir, and the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed the emperor's younger uterine half-brother, Prince Yue of Langye, as successor, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 中書令何充曰：「父子相傳，先王舊典，易之者鮮不致亂。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Ling He Chong said, "Father-to-son succession is the ancient royal norm; those who change it rarely escape disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, Director of the Secretariat, said, "Passing the throne from father to son is the ancient royal norm; those who alter it seldom avoid turmoil.

sentences.zh: 故武王不授聖弟，非不愛也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wu did not give the throne to his sage younger brother—not from lack of love.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu did not enthrone his gifted younger brother—not because he loved him less.

sentences.zh: 今琅邪踐阼，將如孺子何！

translations.literal: If Langye now ascends the throne, what is to become of the infant sons!"
translations.idiomatic: If Prince Langye takes the throne, what will become of these infant princes!"

sentences.zh: 」冰不聽。

translations.literal: " Bing would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Bing would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 下詔，以岳為嗣，並以弈繼琅邪哀王。

translations.literal: An edict was issued making Yue the heir and also assigning Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Yue as heir and assigned Yi to succeed the late Prince Ai of Langye.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，冰、充及武陵王晞、會稽王昱、尚書令諸葛恢並受顧命。

translations.literal: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Shangshu Ling Zhuge Hui all received the dying emperor's charge.
translations.idiomatic: On rénchén, Bing, Chong, Prince Xi of Wuling, Prince Yu of Kuaiji, and Zhuge Hui, Director of the Secretariat, all received the emperor's deathbed commission.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝崩。

translations.literal: On guǐsì, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On guǐsì the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 帝幼沖嗣位，不親庶政；

translations.literal: The emperor had succeeded young and did not personally handle routine government;
translations.idiomatic: He had come to the throne as a child and had not personally directed routine affairs;

sentences.zh: 及長，頗有勤儉之德。

translations.literal: when he grew up he showed considerable virtue in diligence and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: but as he matured he showed real virtue in diligence and frugality.

sentences.zh: 甲午，琅邪王即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: On jiǎwǔ, the Prince of Langye assumed the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiǎwǔ Prince Yue of Langye ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 己亥，封成帝子丕為琅邪王，弈為東海王。

translations.literal: On jǐhài, the late Emperor Cheng's son Pi was enfeoffed as Prince of Langye and Yi as Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: On jǐhài the new emperor enfeoffed the late Emperor Cheng's son Pi as Prince of Langye and Yi as Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 康帝亮陰不言，委政於庾冰、何充。

translations.literal: Emperor Kang observed mourning in silence and entrusted government to Yu Bing and He Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang observed mourning in silence and left government to Yu Bing and He Chong.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰，葬成帝於興平陵。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bǐngchén, Emperor Cheng was buried at Xingping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on bǐngchén, Emperor Cheng was buried at Xingping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 帝徒行送喪，至閶闔門，乃升素輿至陵所。

translations.literal: The emperor walked on foot in the funeral procession; only at the Changhe Gate did he mount a plain carriage to the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked on foot behind the bier and mounted a plain carriage only at the Changhe Gate for the ride to the tomb.

sentences.zh: 既葬，帝臨軒，庾冰、何充侍坐。

translations.literal: After the burial the emperor took the throne; Yu Bing and He Chong sat in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial the emperor held court, with Yu Bing and He Chong in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕嗣鴻業，二君之力也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have inherited the great enterprise—this is thanks to you two ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have inherited the great enterprise—it is thanks to you two ministers."

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「陛下龍飛，臣冰之力也；

translations.literal: " Chong said, "When Your Majesty ascended the dragon throne, it was Minister Bing's doing;
translations.idiomatic: " Chong said, "When Your Majesty ascended the throne, it was Minister Bing's doing;

sentences.zh: 若如臣議，不睹昇平之世。

translations.literal: had you followed my counsel, you would not have seen this age of rising peace."
translations.idiomatic: had you followed my counsel, you would not be living to see this peaceful age."

sentences.zh: 」帝有慚色。

translations.literal: " The emperor showed a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 己未，以充為驃騎將軍、都督徐州、揚州之晉陵諸軍事、領徐州刺史，鎮京口，避諸庾也。

translations.literal: On jǐwèi, Chong was made Biaoqi General, commander of Jinling and related military affairs in Xuzhou and Yangzhou, and concurrently Inspector of Xuzhou, stationed at Jingkou to keep clear of the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: On jǐwèi Chong was appointed Biaoqi General with command over Jinling and related forces in Xuzhou and Yangzhou, and concurrently made inspector of Xuzhou with his seat at Jingkou—partly to keep him away from the Yu family.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，燕王皝遷都龍城，赦其境內。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, moved his capital to Longcheng and pardoned those within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Murong Huang, prince of Yan, moved his capital to Longcheng and granted an amnesty within his realm.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍翰言於皝曰：「宇文強盛日久，屢為國患。

translations.literal: Jianwei General Han said to Huang, "The Yuwen have been strong for a long time and have repeatedly been a scourge to our state.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwei General Murong Han said to Huang, "The Yuwen have grown strong over many years and have repeatedly threatened our state.

sentences.zh: 今逸豆歸篡竊得國，群情不附。

translations.literal: Now Yidougui seized the realm by usurpation and the people are not attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui has now usurped the throne, and the tribes do not stand behind him.

sentences.zh: 加之性識庸暗，將帥非才，國無防衛，軍無部伍。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature and judgment are dull and dim; his commanders lack talent; the state has no defense and the army no proper formations.
translations.idiomatic: He is dull and shortsighted, his commanders are incompetent, the realm lacks proper defenses, and the army lacks disciplined formations.

sentences.zh: 臣久在其國，悉其地形；

translations.literal: Your servant long dwelt in their country and knows their terrain thoroughly;
translations.idiomatic: I lived long in their country and know their terrain well;

sentences.zh: 雖遠附強羯，聲勢不接，無益救援；

translations.literal: though they lean on the powerful Jie from afar, their forces do not connect and cannot aid them;
translations.idiomatic: though they court the powerful Jie from afar, those allies are too distant to help in time;

sentences.zh: 今若擊之，百舉百克。

translations.literal: if we strike now, we will prevail in every hundred attempts.
translations.idiomatic: if we strike now, we will prevail at every turn.

sentences.zh: 然高句麗去國密邇，常有闚□之志。

translations.literal: Yet Koguryŏ lies close to our capital and has long harbored designs of encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Koguryŏ lies close to our heartland and has long harbored designs against us.

sentences.zh: 彼知宇文既亡，禍將及己，必乘虛深入，掩吾不備。

translations.literal: When they know the Yuwen are destroyed, disaster will reach them too; they are sure to exploit our opening and strike deep while we are unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Once they see the Yuwen destroyed, they will know they are next and will surely exploit our absence to strike deep while our guard is down.

sentences.zh: 若少留兵則不足以守，多留兵則不足以行。

translations.literal: If we leave few troops they will not suffice to hold; if we leave many, the campaign force will not suffice to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Leave too few troops behind and we cannot hold our ground; leave too many and the field army cannot march.

sentences.zh: 此心腹之患也，宜先除之；

translations.literal: This is a danger to the heart and belly; we should eliminate it first;
translations.idiomatic: This is the danger at our vitals; we should eliminate it first.

sentences.zh: 觀其勢力，一舉可克。

translations.literal: judging their strength, they can be taken in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Judging their strength, they can be taken in a single campaign.

sentences.zh: 宇文自守之虜，必不能遠來爭利。

translations.literal: The Yuwen are a tribe that only defends itself and surely will not come from afar to contest the prize.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen are a defensive people and will not march far to contest the outcome.

sentences.zh: 既取高句麗，還取宇文，如返手耳。

translations.literal: Once Koguryŏ is taken, turning back to take the Yuwen is like turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once Koguryŏ is taken, turning to crush the Yuwen will be as easy as turning one's hand.

sentences.zh: 二國既平，利盡東海，國富兵強，無返顧之憂，然後中原可圖也。

translations.literal: When both states are pacified, the profit of the eastern sea will be ours, the state rich and the army strong, with no worry of looking back—then the Central Plains may be contemplated."
translations.idiomatic: With both realms subdued, we will hold the wealth of the eastern sea, our state will be rich and our army strong, and with no enemy at our rear we may then turn toward the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 」皝曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Huang said, "Excellent!
translations.idiomatic: " Huang said, "Excellent!

sentences.zh: 」將擊高句麗。

translations.literal: " He was about to attack Koguryŏ.
translations.idiomatic: " He prepared to attack Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 高句麗有二道，其北道平闊，南道險狹，眾欲從北道。

translations.literal: Koguryŏ had two routes: the northern road was broad and level, the southern narrow and perilous; the host wished to take the northern road.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ could be reached by two routes—the northern broad and open, the southern narrow and perilous—and the army favored the northern road.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「虜以常情料之，必謂大軍從北道，當重北而輕南。

translations.literal: Han said, "The barbarians, judging by ordinary expectation, will surely think the great army will come by the northern road and will strengthen the north while slighting the south.
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "The enemy, thinking as men usually do, will expect our main force on the northern road and will mass their strength in the north while neglecting the south.

sentences.zh: 王宜帥銳兵從南道擊之，出其不意，丸都不足取也。

translations.literal: Your Highness should lead elite troops by the southern road to strike them; catching them unawares, Wandu will not be hard to take.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should lead picked troops by the southern road and take them unawares—Wandu will not be hard to seize.

sentences.zh: 別遣偏師出北道，縱有蹉跌，其腹心己潰，四支無能為也。

translations.literal: Send a separate detachment out the northern road; even if it meets setbacks, once their heart is broken their limbs can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Send a secondary force along the northern road; even if it stumbles, once their heartland is broken their extremities can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 」皝從之。

translations.literal: " Huang followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，皝自將勁兵四萬出南道，以慕容翰、慕容霸為前鋒，別遣長史王寓等將兵萬五千出北道，以伐高句麗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Huang personally led forty thousand crack troops out the southern road, with Murong Han and Murong Ba as vanguard, and separately sent Chief Clerk Wang Yu and others with fifteen thousand men out the northern road to attack Koguryŏ.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Huang led forty thousand picked troops in person along the southern route, with Murong Han and Murong Ba as vanguard, while Chief Clerk Wang Yu and others took fifteen thousand men along the northern route against Koguryŏ.

sentences.zh: 高句麗王釗果遣弟武帥精兵五萬拒北道，自帥羸兵以備南道。

translations.literal: King Chao of Koguryŏ indeed sent his brother Wu at the head of fifty thousand elite troops to block the northern road, while he himself led weak troops to guard the southern road.
translations.idiomatic: King Chao of Koguryŏ duly sent his brother Wu with fifty thousand elite troops to block the northern road, while he himself led weaker forces to face the south.

sentences.zh: 慕容翰等先至，與釗合戰，皝以大眾繼之。

translations.literal: Murong Han and the others arrived first and joined battle with Chao; Huang followed with the main host.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han's vanguard arrived first and engaged Chao; Huang came up with the main army.

sentences.zh: 左常侍鮮于亮曰：「臣以俘虜蒙王國士之恩，不可以不報；

translations.literal: Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xianyu Liang said, "Your servant, though once a captive, received the grace of the state's favor and cannot fail to repay it;
translations.idiomatic: Left Attendant-in-Ordinary Xianyu Liang said, "I was once a captive, yet Your Majesty treated me as a pillar of the state; I cannot fail to repay that debt;

sentences.zh: 今日，臣死日也！

translations.literal: today is the day your servant dies!"
translations.idiomatic: today is the day I die!"

sentences.zh: 」獨與數騎先犯高句麗陣，所向摧陷。

translations.literal: " He alone with a few horsemen was first to charge the Koguryŏ line, breaking through wherever he turned.
translations.idiomatic: " He charged the Koguryŏ line at the head of only a few horsemen and broke through wherever he struck.

sentences.zh: 高句麗陣動，大眾因而乘之，高句麗兵大敗。

translations.literal: The Koguryŏ formation wavered; the great host pressed the advantage and the Koguryŏ army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Koguryŏ line buckled; the main army pressed the advantage and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 左長史韓壽斬高句麗將阿佛和度加，諸軍乘勝追之，遂入丸都。

translations.literal: Left Chief Clerk Han Shou slew the Koguryŏ general Afohedujia; the armies pursued in victory and entered Wandu.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chief Clerk Han Shou slew the Koguryŏ general Afohedujia; the armies pursued the victory and entered Wandu.

sentences.zh: 釗單騎走，輕車將軍慕輿泥追獲其母周氏及妻而還。

translations.literal: Chao fled alone on horseback; Light-Carriage General Murong Ni pursued and captured his mother Lady Zhou and his wife before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled alone; Light-Carriage General Murong Ni pursued and captured his mother, Lady Zhou, and his wife before returning.

sentences.zh: 會王寓等戰於北道，皆敗沒，由是皝不復窮追。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Wang Yu and the others fought on the northern road and were all defeated and lost; for this reason Huang did not press the pursuit to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Yu's force on the northern road was destroyed; for that reason Huang did not press the pursuit further.

sentences.zh: 遣使招釗，釗不出。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to summon Chao; Chao did not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to summon Chao, but Chao would not submit.

sentences.zh: 皝將還，韓壽曰：「高句麗之地，不可戍守。

translations.literal: As Huang was about to withdraw, Han Shou said, "The land of Koguryŏ cannot be garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: As Huang prepared to withdraw, Han Shou said, "Koguryŏ cannot be held by garrisons.

sentences.zh: 今其主亡民散，潛伏山谷；

translations.literal: Now their ruler is fled and the people scattered, hiding in mountain valleys;
translations.idiomatic: Their king has fled and the people are scattered in the hills;

sentences.zh: 大軍既去，必復鳩聚，收其餘燼，猶足為患。

translations.literal: once the great army departs they will surely gather again; gathering the embers that remain, they will still be enough to cause trouble.
translations.idiomatic: once our army leaves they will rally again, and even the embers they gather will be enough to trouble us.

sentences.zh: 請載其父屍、囚其生母而歸，俟其束身自歸，然後返之，撫以恩信，策之上也。

translations.literal: I ask that we carry off his father's corpse and take his living mother prisoner; wait until he binds himself and comes to surrender, then return them and treat him with favor and trust—this is the supreme stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: Carry off his father's corpse and take his mother prisoner; when he comes to surrender in person, return them and win him with kindness and trust—that is the best policy."

sentences.zh: 」皝從之。

translations.literal: " Huang followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Huang agreed.

sentences.zh: 發釗父乙弗利墓。

translations.literal: They opened the tomb of Chao's father Yifuli.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the tomb of Chao's father Yifuli.

sentences.zh: 載其屍，收其府庫累世之寶，虜男女五萬餘口，燒其宮室，毀丸都城而還。

translations.literal: They carried off the corpse, seized the treasures accumulated in the royal storehouses for generations, captured more than fifty thousand men and women, burned the palaces, destroyed the walls of Wandu, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They carried off the corpse, seized the hoarded treasures of generations, took more than fifty thousand captives, burned the palaces, razed the walls of Wandu, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬子，立妃褚氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on rénzǐ, Consort Chu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on rénzǐ, Lady Chu was made empress.

sentences.zh: 征豫章太守褚裒為侍中、尚書。

translations.literal: Chu Pou, Administrator of Yuzhang, was summoned as Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pou, the administrator of Yuzhang, was summoned to serve as Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 裒自以後父，不願居中任事，苦求外出；

translations.literal: Pou, considering himself the empress's father by marriage, was unwilling to hold a central post and importunately sought an outside appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Pou, as the empress's father by marriage, did not wish to hold office at court and pleaded repeatedly for an outside post;

sentences.zh: 乃除建威將軍、江州刺史，鎮半洲。

translations.literal: he was therefore made Jianwei General and Inspector of Jiangzhou, stationed at Banzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and was appointed Jianwei General and inspector of Jiangzhou with his seat at Banzhou.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎作台觀四十餘所於鄴，又營洛陽、長安二宮，作者四十餘萬人；

translations.literal: Prince Hu of Zhao built more than forty terraces and towers at Ye, and also constructed palaces at Luoyang and Chang'an; those pressed into labor numbered more than four hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu, prince of Zhao, built more than forty terraces and towers at Ye and also raised palaces at Luoyang and Chang'an, pressing more than four hundred thousand men into labor;

sentences.zh: 又欲自鄴起閣道至襄國，敕河南四州治南伐之備，並、朔、秦、雍嚴西討之資，青、冀、幽州為東征之計，皆三五發卒。

translations.literal: he also wished to raise an elevated causeway from Ye to Xiangguo, ordered the four provinces of Henan to prepare for a southern campaign, Bing, Shuo, Qin, and Yong to stock supplies for a western expedition, and Qing, Ji, and You for an eastern campaign—everywhere drafting three men in five.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned an elevated causeway from Ye to Xiangguo, ordered the four Henan provinces to prepare for a southern campaign, Bing, Shuo, Qin, and Yong to stock a western expedition, and Qing, Ji, and You an eastern one—everywhere conscripting three men in five.

sentences.zh: 諸州軍造甲者五十餘萬人，船夫十七萬人，為水所沒，虎狼所食者三分居一。

translations.literal: In the provinces more than five hundred thousand men forged armor for the army and one hundred seventy thousand served as boatmen; of these, one in three perished by drowning or by tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred thousand men across the provinces forged armor for the armies, and one hundred seventy thousand served as boatmen; of them, one man in three died by drowning or by tiger and wolf.

sentences.zh: 加之公侯、牧宰競營私利，百姓失業愁困。

translations.literal: Moreover dukes, marquises, and regional governors all scrambled for private gain, and the common people lost their livelihoods in grief and distress.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this, nobles and regional governors scrambled for private gain, and the common people lost their livelihoods in misery.

sentences.zh: 貝丘人李弘因眾心之怨，自言姓名應讖，連結黨與，署置百寮；

translations.literal: Li Hong of Beiqiu, exploiting popular resentment, declared that his name fulfilled a prophecy, formed a faction, and appointed a full set of officials;
translations.idiomatic: Li Hong of Beiqiu, exploiting popular resentment, declared that his name fulfilled a prophecy, gathered followers, and appointed a full roster of officials;

sentences.zh: 事發，誅之，連坐者數千家。

translations.literal: When the affair broke, he was executed, and several thousand households were implicated by association.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, he was put to death, and several thousand households were punished along with him.

sentences.zh: 虎畋獵無度，晨出夜歸，又多微行，躬察作役。

translations.literal: Hu hunted without measure, leaving at dawn and returning at night; he also often went in disguise to inspect construction labor in person.
translations.idiomatic: Hu hunted without restraint, setting out at dawn and returning at night, and often went in disguise to inspect construction projects himself.

sentences.zh: 侍中京兆韋謏諫曰：「陛下忽天下之重，輕行斤斧之間，猝有狂夫之變，雖有智勇，將安所施！

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wei Xu of Jingzhao remonstrated: "Your Majesty neglects the weight of the realm, lightly walking among axes and hatchets; if a madman strikes suddenly, though you have wisdom and courage, where could you apply them!
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wei Xu of Jingzhao remonstrated: "Your Majesty neglects the weight of empire and walks lightly among common laborers; if some madman should strike, where could even wisdom and courage avail you!

sentences.zh: 又興役無時，廢民耘獲，吁嗟盈路，殆非仁聖之所忍為也。

translations.literal: Moreover you launch projects without season, abandoning the people's plowing and harvest; lamentation fills the roads—this is scarcely what a benevolent sage could bear to do."
translations.idiomatic: You also launch projects without regard to season, leaving the people unable to farm or harvest; lamentation fills the roads—this is scarcely what a benevolent ruler could endure."

sentences.zh: 」虎賜謏谷帛，而興繕滋繁，游察自若。

translations.literal: " Hu rewarded Xu with grain and silk, yet construction grew ever more lavish and his tours and inspections continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu rewarded Xu with grain and silk, yet construction grew ever more lavish and his tours and inspections continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 秦公韜有寵於虎，太子宣惡之。

translations.literal: Duke of Qin, Tao, enjoyed Hu's favor, and the heir apparent Xuan hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Tao of Qin enjoyed Shi Hu's favor, and the heir apparent Xuan hated him.

sentences.zh: 右僕射張離領五兵尚書，欲求媚於宣，說之曰：「今諸侯吏兵過限，宜漸裁省，以壯本根。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhang Li, who also headed the Masters of the Five Armies, wished to curry favor with Xuan and said to him, "The officials and troops of the feudal lords now exceed their limits; they should be gradually reduced to strengthen the root."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Zhang Li, who also headed the Masters of the Five Armies, sought to curry favor with Xuan and told him, "The officials and troops of the feudal princes now exceed their limits and should be gradually cut back to strengthen the throne."

sentences.zh: 」宣使離為奏：「秦、燕、義陽、樂平四公，聽置吏一百九十七人，帳下兵二百人；

translations.literal: " Xuan had Li memorialize: "The four dukes of Qin, Yan, Yiyang, and Leping may each appoint one hundred ninety-seven officials and two hundred personal guards;
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan had Li submit a memorial: "The four dukes of Qin, Yan, Yiyang, and Leping may each appoint one hundred ninety-seven officials and keep two hundred personal guards;

sentences.zh: 自是以下，三分置一，餘兵五萬，悉配東宮。

translations.literal: below that rank, one-third of the present establishment; the remaining fifty thousand troops are all to be assigned to the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: below them, retain one man in three; the remaining fifty thousand troops are all to be assigned to the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 」於是諸公鹹怨，嫌釁益深矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon all the dukes resented it, and mutual suspicion grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon all the dukes resented the move, and mutual suspicion grew deeper still.

sentences.zh: 青州上言：「濟南平陵城北石虎，一夕移於城東南，有狼狐千餘跡隨之，跡皆成蹊。

translations.literal: Qingzhou reported: "The stone tiger north of Pingling in Jinan moved in a single night to the southeast of the city; more than a thousand tracks of wolves and foxes followed it, and the tracks all became paths."
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou reported: "The stone tiger north of Pingling in Jinan moved overnight to the southeast of the city, followed by more than a thousand wolf and fox tracks that formed paths."

sentences.zh: 」虎喜曰：「石虎者，朕也；

translations.literal: " Hu rejoiced and said, "The stone tiger—that is I;
translations.idiomatic: " Hu rejoiced and said, "The stone tiger—that is I;

sentences.zh: 自西北徙而東南者，天意欲使朕平蕩江南也。

translations.literal: moving from the northwest to the southeast means Heaven intends me to pacify the Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: moving from the northwest to the southeast means Heaven intends me to pacify the south.

sentences.zh: 其敕諸州兵明年悉集，朕當親董六師，以奉天命。

translations.literal: Order all the provinces to muster their troops next year; I shall personally lead the six armies to fulfill Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Order every province to muster its troops next year; I shall personally lead the six armies to fulfill Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆賀，上《皇德頌》者一百七人。

translations.literal: " The ministers all congratulated him, and one hundred seven men presented "Odes to Imperial Virtue."
translations.idiomatic: " The ministers all congratulated him, and one hundred seven men submitted odes to imperial virtue.

sentences.zh: 制：「征士五人出車一乘，牛二頭，米十五斛，絹十匹，調不辦者斬。

translations.literal: An ordinance was issued: "Every five conscripted men must furnish one cart, two oxen, fifteen hu of grain, and ten bolts of silk; those who fail to meet the levy are to be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: He decreed: "Every five conscripted men must furnish one cart, two oxen, fifteen hu of grain, and ten bolts of silk; those who fail to meet the levy are to be beheaded."

sentences.zh: 」民至鬻子以供軍須，猶不能給，自經於道樹者相望。

translations.literal: " The people went so far as to sell their children to meet military needs, yet still could not supply enough; those who hanged themselves from roadside trees were visible one after another.
translations.idiomatic: " The people sold their children to meet military levies and still could not keep up; suicides from roadside trees lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 康皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Kang
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Kang

sentences.zh: 春，二月，高句麗王釗遣其弟稱臣入朝於燕，貢珍異以千數。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, King Chao of Koguryŏ sent his younger brother to present himself as a vassal at the court of Yan, offering thousands of rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, King Chao of Koguryŏ sent his younger brother to submit as a vassal at the court of Yan, offering thousands of rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝乃還其父屍，猶留其母為質。

translations.literal: Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, then returned his father's corpse but still kept his mother as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang then returned his father's corpse but kept his mother as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 宇文逸豆歸遣其相莫淺渾將兵擊燕；

translations.literal: Yidougui of the Yuwen sent his chancellor Mo Qianhun to lead troops against Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui of the Yuwen sent his chancellor Mo Qianhun to attack Yan with an army;

sentences.zh: 諸將爭欲擊之，燕王皝不許。

translations.literal: the generals all vied to strike him, but Murong Huang would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the generals all clamored to attack, but Murong Huang refused.

sentences.zh: 莫淺渾以為皝畏之，酣飲縱獵，不復設備。

translations.literal: Mo Qianhun thought Huang feared him, drank heavily, hunted freely, and no longer made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Qianhun concluded that Huang feared him, drank heavily, hunted at will, and ceased all precautions.

sentences.zh: 皝使慕容輸出擊之，莫淺渾大敗，僅以身免，盡俘其眾。

translations.literal: Huang sent Murong Yu to strike; Mo Qianhun was utterly defeated, barely escaping with his life, and all his troops were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Huang sent Murong Yu to attack; Mo Qianhun was routed, barely escaping with his life, and his entire force was captured.

sentences.zh: 庾翼為人慷慨，喜功名，不尚浮華。

translations.literal: Yu Yi was generous by nature, fond of merit and fame, and did not esteem empty display.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi was openhanded by nature, eager for achievement and renown, and scorned empty display.

sentences.zh: 琅邪內史桓溫，彝之子也，尚南康公主，豪爽有風概。

translations.literal: Huan Wen, Administrator of Langye, was the son of Huan Yi; he married the Princess of Nankang and was bold and open with a commanding presence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, administrator of Langye, was the son of Huan Yi; he had married the Princess of Nankang and was bold, open, and commanding in bearing.

sentences.zh: 翼與之友善，相期以寧濟海內。

translations.literal: Yi was on friendly terms with him and they pledged together to bring peace to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yi befriended him, and they pledged together to bring peace to the realm.

sentences.zh: 翼嘗薦溫於成帝曰：「桓溫有英雄之才，願陛下勿以常人遇之，常婿畜之。

translations.literal: Yi once recommended Wen to Emperor Cheng, saying, "Huan Wen has the talent of a hero; I hope Your Majesty will not treat him as an ordinary man or keep him as a son-in-law in the household.
translations.idiomatic: Yi once recommended Wen to Emperor Cheng, saying, "Huan Wen has heroic talent; I beg Your Majesty not to treat him as an ordinary man or keep him merely as a son-in-law at court.

sentences.zh: 宜委以方、邵之任，必有弘濟艱難之勳」。

translations.literal: Entrust him with duties like those of Fang Shu and Shao Hu, and he is sure to achieve great merit in delivering the state through hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Entrust him with duties like those of Fang Shu and Shao Hu, and he will surely achieve great merit in delivering the state through hardship."

sentences.zh: 時杜乂、殷浩並才名冠世，冀獨弗之重也，曰：「此輩宜束之高閣，俟天下太平，然後徐議其任耳。

translations.literal: At the time Du Yi and Yin Hao both topped the world in talent and reputation, but Yi alone did not esteem them highly, saying, "These men should be shut away on a high shelf; wait until the realm is at peace, then slowly discuss their appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Du Yi and Yin Hao were famed above all others for talent, but Yi alone did not esteem them, saying, "These men should be shelved until the realm is at peace; only then should we discuss their appointments.

sentences.zh: 「浩累辭征辟，屏居墓所，幾將十年，時人擬之管、葛。

translations.literal: " Hao repeatedly declined summons to office and lived in seclusion at his father's tomb for nearly ten years; men of the time compared him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao had repeatedly declined office and lived in seclusion at his father's tomb for nearly ten years; contemporaries compared him to Guan Zhong and Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 江夏相謝尚、長山令王濛常伺其出處，以卜江左興亡。

translations.literal: Xie Shang, Administrator of Jiangxia, and Wang Meng, Magistrate of Changshan, often watched whether he would emerge or remain in seclusion, taking it as an omen of the rise or fall of the Jiangzuo regime.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Shang, administrator of Jiangxia, and Wang Meng, magistrate of Changshan, often watched whether he would emerge from seclusion, taking it as an omen of the south's rise or fall.

sentences.zh: 嘗相與省之，知浩有確然之志，既返，相謂曰：「深源不起，當如蒼生何！

translations.literal: They once visited him together and saw that Hao had a firm resolve; on their return they said to each other, "If Shenyuan does not rise, what is to become of the common people!"
translations.idiomatic: They once visited him together and saw that Hao was firmly resolved to remain apart; on their return they said to each other, "If Shenyuan does not take office, what is to become of the people!"

sentences.zh: 」尚，鯤之子也。

translations.literal: " Shang was the son of Xie Kun.
translations.idiomatic: " Shang was the son of Xie Kun.

sentences.zh: 翼請浩為司馬；

translations.literal: Yi invited Hao to serve as Marshal;
translations.idiomatic: Yi invited Hao to serve as marshal;

sentences.zh: 詔除侍中、安西軍司，浩不應。

translations.literal: an edict appointed him Palace Attendant and Army Aide of the Anxi command, but Hao did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: the court appointed him Palace Attendant and army aide of the Anxi command, but Hao declined.

sentences.zh: 翼遺浩書曰：「王夷甫立名非真，雖雲談道，實長華競。

translations.literal: Yi sent Hao a letter saying, "Wang Yifu made a name that was not genuine; though he spoke of the Way, in truth he fostered empty rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote to Hao: "Wang Yifu won a reputation that was not genuine; though he spoke of the Way, he in truth fostered empty rivalry.

sentences.zh: 明德君子，遇會處際，寧可然乎！

translations.literal: Can a bright and virtuous gentleman, meeting his moment and place, act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Can a bright and virtuous gentleman, meeting his moment, act thus!"

sentences.zh: 」浩猶不起。

translations.literal: " Hao still would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao still refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 殷羨為長沙相，在郡貪殘，庾冰與翼書屬之。

translations.literal: Yin Xian was Administrator of Changsha and was greedy and cruel in the commandery; Yu Bing wrote to Yi asking him to look after him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Xian, administrator of Changsha, was greedy and cruel in his commandery; Yu Bing wrote to Yi asking him to protect him.

sentences.zh: 翼報曰：「殷君驕豪，亦似由有佳兒，弟故小令物情容之。

translations.literal: Yi replied, "Master Yin is proud and overbearing—perhaps because he has a fine son; for that reason, brother, you have slightly indulged popular feeling in tolerating him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "Master Yin is proud and overbearing—perhaps because he has a fine son; for that reason, brother, you have indulged popular feeling in tolerating him.

sentences.zh: 大較江東之政，以嫗煦豪強，常為民蠹；

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, government east of the Yangzi coddles the powerful and they constantly become parasites on the people;
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, government east of the Yangzi coddles the powerful, who constantly prey on the people;

sentences.zh: 時有行法，輒施之寒劣。

translations.literal: when the law is applied at all, it is applied only to the poor and weak.
translations.idiomatic: when the law is applied at all, it falls only on the poor and weak.

sentences.zh: 如往年偷石頭倉米一百萬斛，皆是豪將輩，而直殺倉督監以塞責。

translations.literal: For example, when a million hu of grain were stolen from the Shitou granary last year, the culprits were all powerful generals, yet only the granary supervisor was killed to satisfy accountability.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, for example, when a million hu of grain were stolen from the Shitou granary, the culprits were powerful generals, yet only the granary supervisor was executed to satisfy accountability.

sentences.zh: 山遐為餘姚長，為官出豪強所藏二千戶，而眾共驅之，令遐不得安席。

translations.literal: Shan Xia was Magistrate of Yuyao and exposed two thousand hidden households among the powerful for taxation, yet the crowd together drove him off and would not let Xia sit in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xia, magistrate of Yuyao, exposed two thousand hidden households among the powerful for taxation, yet the powerful together drove him out and left him no peace.

sentences.zh: 雖皆前宰之惛謬，江東事去，實此之由。

translations.literal: Though all this stems from the folly of former chief ministers, the loss of Jiangdong's cause is truly due to this.
translations.idiomatic: Though all this stems from the folly of former chief ministers, the south's decline is truly due to this.

sentences.zh: 兄弟不幸，橫陷此中，自不能拔足於風塵之外，當共明目而治之。

translations.literal: We brothers are unhappily caught in this ourselves and cannot pull free of the dust and turmoil; we should together govern with clear eyes.
translations.idiomatic: We brothers are unhappily caught in this ourselves and cannot escape the dust and turmoil; we should govern together with clear eyes.

sentences.zh: 荊州所統二十餘郡，唯長沙最惡；

translations.literal: Of the more than twenty commanderies under Jingzhou, Changsha alone is the worst;
translations.idiomatic: Of the more than twenty commanderies under Jingzhou, Changsha is the worst;

sentences.zh: 惡而不黜，與殺督監者復何異邪！

translations.literal: if he is wicked and not removed, how is that different from killing the granary supervisor!"
translations.idiomatic: if he is wicked and not removed, how is that different from killing the granary supervisor!"

sentences.zh: 」遐，簡之子也。

translations.literal: " Xia was the son of Shan Jian.
translations.idiomatic: " Xia was the son of Shan Jian.

sentences.zh: 翼以滅胡取蜀為己任，遣使東約燕王皝，西約張駿，刻期大舉。

translations.literal: Yi took the destruction of the barbarians and the seizure of Shu as his personal mission, sent envoys east to treat with Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, and west with Zhang Jun, fixing a date for a great campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yi made the destruction of the barbarians and the conquest of Shu his personal mission, sent envoys east to treat with Murong Huang and west with Zhang Jun, and set a date for a great campaign.

sentences.zh: 朝議多以為難，唯庾冰意與之同，而桓溫、譙王無忌皆贊成之。

translations.literal: Court discussion mostly regarded it as difficult; only Yu Bing's view agreed with his, while Huan Wen and Prince Wuji of Qiao all supported it.
translations.idiomatic: Most at court thought the plan difficult; only Yu Bing agreed with him, while Huan Wen and Prince Wuji of Qiao supported it.

sentences.zh: 無忌，承之子也。

translations.literal: Wuji was the son of Sima Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji was the son of Sima Cheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，趙汝南太守戴開帥數千人詣翼降。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Dai Kai, Administrator of Runan in Zhao, led several thousand men to Yi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Dai Kai, the Runan administrator in Zhao, led several thousand men to surrender to Yi.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，下詔議經略中原。

translations.literal: On dīngsì, an edict was issued to discuss strategy for the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: On dīngsì the court issued an edict to discuss strategy for recovering the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 翼欲悉所部之眾北伐，表桓宣為都督司、雍、梁三州、荊州之四郡諸軍事、梁州刺史，前趣丹水；

translations.literal: Yi wished to lead all the forces under his command north in campaign and memorialized that Huan Xuan be made commander of military affairs in Si, Yong, and Liang provinces and four commanderies of Jingzhou, and Inspector of Liangzhou, to advance first toward Danshui;
translations.idiomatic: Yi wished to lead all his forces north and memorialized that Huan Xuan be made commander of Si, Yong, and Liang and four Jingzhou commanderies, with the title inspector of Liangzhou, to advance first toward Danshui;

sentences.zh: 桓溫為前鋒小督、假節，帥眾入臨淮；

translations.literal: Huan Wen was made junior commander of the vanguard with provisional credentials and led his troops into Linhuai;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was made junior vanguard commander with provisional credentials and led his troops into Linhuai;

sentences.zh: 並發所統六州奴及車牛驢馬，百姓嗟怒。

translations.literal: at the same time all the bondsmen, carts, oxen, donkeys, and horses of the six provinces under his command were levied, and the common people groaned in anger.
translations.idiomatic: at the same time all the bondsmen, carts, oxen, donkeys, and horses of the six provinces under his command were levied, and the people groaned in anger.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍復求婚於燕，燕王皝使納馬千匹為禮；

translations.literal: Tuoba Shiyijian, King of Dai, again sought marriage with Yan; Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, had a thousand horses sent as bride-price;
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Shiyijian, king of Dai, again sought marriage with Yan; Murong Huang had a thousand horses sent as bride-price;

sentences.zh: 什翼犍不與，又倨慢無子婿禮。

translations.literal: Shiyijian would not give them and moreover was arrogant and remiss in the rites due a son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian refused them and moreover behaved arrogantly, neglecting the rites due a son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 八月，皝遣世子俊帥前軍師評等擊代。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Huang sent the heir apparent Jun at the head of Front Army Commander Ping and others to attack Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Huang sent the heir apparent Jun with Front Army Commander Ping and others to attack Dai.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍帥眾避去，燕人無所見而還。

translations.literal: Shiyijian led his forces away to avoid them, and the men of Yan saw no one and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian led his forces away to avoid battle, and the Yan army found no one and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 漢主壽卒，謚曰昭文，廟號中宗；

translations.literal: The Han ruler Shou died; his posthumous title was Zhaowen and his temple name Zhongzong;
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler Shou died; his posthumous title was Zhaowen and his temple name Zhongzong;

sentences.zh: 太子勢即位，大赦。

translations.literal: the heir apparent Shi succeeded to the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: the heir apparent Shi succeeded to the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 趙太子宣擊鮮卑斛谷提，大破之，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: Xuan, heir apparent of Zhao, attacked the Xianbei chief Hugu Ti, defeated him utterly, and took thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xuan, heir apparent of Zhao, attacked the Xianbei chief Hugu Ti, routed him, and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 宇文逸豆歸執段遼弟蘭，送於趙，並獻駿馬萬匹。

translations.literal: Yidougui of the Yuwen seized Duan Liao's younger brother Lan, sent him to Zhao, and also presented ten thousand fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui of the Yuwen seized Duan Liao's younger brother Lan, sent him to Zhao, and also presented ten thousand fine horses.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎命蘭帥所從鮮卑五千人屯令支。

translations.literal: Shi Hu, Prince of Zhao, ordered Lan to lead the five thousand Xianbei who accompanied him to garrison Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu ordered Lan to lead the five thousand Xianbei who accompanied him to garrison Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 庾翼欲移鎮襄陽，恐朝廷不許，乃奏雲移鎮安陸。

translations.literal: Yu Yi wished to move his headquarters to Xiangyang but feared the court would not permit it, so he memorialized that the cloud omens required moving the garrison to Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi wished to move his headquarters to Xiangyang but feared the court would refuse, so he memorialized that omens required moving the garrison to Anlu.

sentences.zh: 帝及朝士皆遣使譬止翼，翼遂違詔北行；

translations.literal: The emperor and court officials all sent envoys to admonish and stop Yi, but Yi defied the edict and marched north;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and court officials all sent envoys to admonish him, but Yi defied the edict and marched north;

sentences.zh: 至夏口，復上表請鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: reaching Xiakou, he again submitted a memorial requesting to be stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: reaching Xiakou, he again submitted a memorial requesting to be stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 翼時有眾四萬，詔加翼都督征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Yi then had forty thousand men under him, and an edict added to his titles Commander of all Campaign and Punitive Forces.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then commanded forty thousand men, and an edict made him commander of all campaign and punitive forces.

sentences.zh: 先是車騎將軍、揚州刺史庾冰屢求出外，辛巳，以冰都督荊、江、寧、益、梁、交、廣七州、豫州之四郡諸軍事，領江州刺史，假節，鎮武昌，以為翼繼援。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu Bing, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou, had repeatedly sought an outside post; on xīnsì he was made commander of military affairs in the seven provinces of Jing, Jiang, Ning, Yi, Liang, Jiao, and Guang and four commanderies of Yuzhou, concurrently Inspector of Jiangzhou with provisional credentials, stationed at Wuchang as reinforcement for Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu Bing, General of Chariots and Cavalry and inspector of Yangzhou, had repeatedly sought an outside post; on xīnsì he was made commander of Jing, Jiang, Ning, Yi, Liang, Jiao, and Guang and four Yuzhou commanderies, concurrently inspector of Jiangzhou with provisional credentials, stationed at Wuchang to reinforce Yi.

sentences.zh: 征徐州刺史何充為督揚、豫、徐州之琅邪諸軍事，領揚州刺史，錄尚書事，輔政。

translations.literal: He Chong, Inspector of Xuzhou, was summoned as commander of military affairs in Yang, Yu, and Xuzhou and the Langye region, concurrently Inspector of Yangzhou, with authority to record affairs of the Masters of Writing and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, inspector of Xuzhou, was summoned as commander of Yang, Yu, and Xuzhou and the Langye region, concurrently made inspector of Yangzhou with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs and assist in government.

sentences.zh: 以琅邪內史桓溫為都督青、徐、兗三州諸軍事、徐州刺史，征江州刺史褚裒為衛將軍，領中書令。

translations.literal: Huan Wen, Administrator of Langye, was made commander of military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces and Inspector of Xuzhou; Chu Pou, Inspector of Jiangzhou, was summoned as Defender General and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen, administrator of Langye, was made commander of Qing, Xu, and Yan and inspector of Xuzhou; Chu Pou, inspector of Jiangzhou, was summoned as Defender General and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，己巳，大赦。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on jǐsì, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the eleventh month, on jǐsì, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，趙王虎享群臣於太武殿，有白雁百餘集馬道之南，虎命射之，皆不獲。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Shi Hu, Prince of Zhao, feasted the ministers in the Hall of Grand Martiality; more than a hundred white wild geese gathered south of the horse path, and Hu ordered them shot, but none were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Shi Hu feasted his ministers in the Hall of Grand Martiality; more than a hundred white wild geese gathered south of the horse path, and Hu ordered them shot, but none were taken.

sentences.zh: 時諸州兵集者百餘萬，太史令趙攬密言於虎曰：「白雁集庭，宮室將空之象，不宜南行。

translations.literal: At the time more than a million troops from the provinces had assembled; Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan secretly told Hu, "White geese gathering in the court is an omen that the palace will be emptied; it is not fitting to march south."
translations.idiomatic: More than a million troops from the provinces had assembled; Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan secretly told Hu, "White geese gathering in the court foretell an emptied palace; it is not fitting to march south."

sentences.zh: 」虎信之，乃臨宣武觀，大閱而罷。

translations.literal: " Hu believed him, then reviewed the troops at the Xuanwu Watchtower on a grand inspection and dismissed the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu believed him, held a grand review at the Xuanwu Watchtower, and dismissed the campaign.

sentences.zh: 漢主勢改元太和，尊母閻氏為皇太后，立妻李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Shi changed the era name to Taihe, honored his mother Lady Yan as empress dowager, and established his wife Lady Li as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler Shi changed the era name to Taihe, honored his mother Lady Yan as empress dowager, and made his wife Lady Li empress.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝與左司馬高詡謀伐宇文逸豆歸。

translations.literal: Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, consulted with Left Marshal Gao Xu on attacking Yidougui of the Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang consulted with Left Marshal Gao Xu on attacking Yidougui of the Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 詡曰：「宇文強盛，今不取，必為國患，伐之必克；

translations.literal: Xu said, "The Yuwen are strong; if we do not take them now they will surely become a scourge to the state, and if we attack we are sure to conquer;
translations.idiomatic: Xu said, "The Yuwen are strong; if we do not take them now they will become a scourge, and if we attack we are sure to prevail;

sentences.zh: 然不利於將。

translations.literal: yet it will not be favorable to the commander."
translations.idiomatic: yet it will not favor the commander."

sentences.zh: 」出而告人曰：「吾往必不返，然忠臣不避也。

translations.literal: " Going out he told others, "I shall surely not return, yet a loyal minister does not shrink from duty."
translations.idiomatic: " Going out he told others, "I shall not return, yet a loyal minister does not shrink from duty."

sentences.zh: 」於是皝自將伐逸豆歸。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Huang personally led the campaign against Yidougui.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Huang personally led the campaign against Yidougui.

sentences.zh: 以慕容翰為前鋒將軍，劉佩副之；

translations.literal: Murong Han was made vanguard general with Liu Pei as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han was made vanguard general with Liu Pei as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 分命慕容軍、慕容恪、慕容霸及折衝將軍慕輿根將兵，三道並進。

translations.literal: Murong Jun, Murong Ke, Murong Ba, and Breaker-of-Ranks General Murong Gen were separately ordered to lead troops in a three-pronged advance.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Jun, Murong Ke, Murong Ba, and Breaker-of-Ranks General Murong Gen were ordered to advance in three columns.

sentences.zh: 高詡將發，不見其妻，使人語以家事而行。

translations.literal: As Gao Xu was about to set out and did not see his wife, he sent someone to speak to her of household affairs and departed.
translations.idiomatic: As Gao Xu was about to set out and did not see his wife, he sent someone to speak to her of household affairs and departed.

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸遣南羅大涉夜干將精兵逆戰，皝遣人馳謂慕容翰曰：「涉夜干勇冠三軍，宜小避之。

translations.literal: Yidougui sent the great chief Sheyegan of Nanluo with elite troops to meet them in battle; Huang sent a messenger in haste to Murong Han, saying, "Sheyegan's courage tops the whole army; you should give him a wide berth."
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui sent the great chief Sheyegan of Nanluo with elite troops to meet them; Huang sent a messenger in haste to Murong Han, saying, "Sheyegan's courage tops the whole army; you should avoid him for the moment."

sentences.zh: 」翰曰：「逸豆歸掃其國內精兵以屬涉夜干，涉夜干素有勇名，一國所賴也。

translations.literal: " Han said, "Yidougui has swept the elite troops of his state and entrusted them to Sheyegan; Sheyegan has long had a name for courage and is the one the whole state relies on.
translations.idiomatic: " Han said, "Yidougui has committed the elite troops of his state to Sheyegan; Sheyegan has long been famed for courage and is the pillar of the whole state.

sentences.zh: 今我克之，其國不攻自潰矣。

translations.literal: If we defeat him now, their state will collapse without our needing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: If we defeat him now, their state will collapse without our needing to attack.

sentences.zh: 且吾孰知涉夜干之為人，雖有虛名，實易與耳，不宜避之，以挫吾兵氣。

translations.literal: Moreover, what do I know of Sheyegan as a man? Though he has an empty reputation, he is in truth easy to deal with; we should not avoid him and damp our army's spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what do I truly know of Sheyegan? Though he has a hollow reputation, he is in truth easy to deal with; we should not avoid him and damp our army's spirit."

sentences.zh: 」遂進戰。

translations.literal: " He then advanced to battle.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advanced to battle.

sentences.zh: 翰自出衝陣，涉夜幹出應之；

translations.literal: Han himself charged the line; Sheyegan came out to meet him;
translations.idiomatic: Han himself charged the enemy line; Sheyegan came out to meet him;

sentences.zh: 慕容容霸從傍邀擊，遂斬涉夜干。

translations.literal: Murong Ba struck from the flank and cut down Sheyegan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ba struck from the flank and cut down Sheyegan.

sentences.zh: 宇文士卒見涉夜干死，不戰而潰；

translations.literal: When the Yuwen soldiers saw Sheyegan dead, they fled without fighting;
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuwen soldiers saw Sheyegan dead, they fled without fighting;

sentences.zh: 燕兵乘勝逐之，遂克其都城。

translations.literal: the Yan army pursued in victory and took their capital.
translations.idiomatic: the Yan army pursued the victory and took their capital.

sentences.zh: 逸豆歸走死漠北，宇文氏由是散亡。

translations.literal: Yidougui fled and died in the northern desert; from this the Yuwen clan was scattered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yidougui fled and died in the northern desert, and the Yuwen clan was scattered and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 皝悉收其畜產、資貨，徙其部眾五千餘落於昌黎，闢地千餘里。

translations.literal: Huang seized all their livestock and goods, moved more than five thousand clans of their people to Changli, and opened more than a thousand li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Huang seized all their livestock and goods, moved more than five thousand clans of their people to Changli, and opened more than a thousand li of territory.

sentences.zh: 更命涉夜干所居城曰威德城，使弟彪戍之而還。

translations.literal: He renamed the city where Sheyegan had dwelt Weide City, left his younger brother Biao to garrison it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the city where Sheyegan had dwelt Weide City, left his younger brother Biao to garrison it, and returned.

sentences.zh: 高詡、劉佩皆中流矢卒。

translations.literal: Gao Xu and Liu Pei both died of wounds from stray arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu and Liu Pei both died of wounds from stray arrows.

sentences.zh: 詡善天文，皝嘗謂曰：「卿有佳書而不見與，何以為忠盡！

translations.literal: Xu was skilled in astronomy; Huang once said to him, "You have excellent books yet do not show them to me—how is that loyalty and devotion!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu was skilled in astronomy. Murong Huang once said to him, "You have excellent books yet do not share them with me—how is that loyal service!"

sentences.zh: 」詡曰：「臣聞人君執要，人臣執職。

translations.literal: " Xu said, "I have heard that the ruler holds to essentials and ministers hold to duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu said, "I have heard that the ruler holds to essentials and ministers hold to their duties.

sentences.zh: 執要者逸，執職者勞。

translations.literal: He who holds essentials is at ease; he who holds duties is worn with labor.
translations.idiomatic: He who holds essentials is at ease; he who holds duties is worn with labor.

sentences.zh: 是以後稷播種，堯不預焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Houji sowed the seed, and Yao did not intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Houji sowed the fields, and Yao did not intervene.

sentences.zh: 占候、天文，晨夜其苦，非至尊之所宜親，殿下將焉用之！

translations.literal: Observing omens and astronomy—its hardship day and night—is not what the Most Exalted should attend to in person; for what would Your Highness use it!"
translations.idiomatic: Observing omens and astronomy is arduous day and night—it is not what the Son of Heaven should attend to in person. What would Your Highness use it for!"

sentences.zh: 」皝默然。

translations.literal: Huang was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Huang fell silent.

sentences.zh: 初，逸豆歸事趙甚謹，貢獻屬路。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yidougui served Zhao with great care; tribute and gifts crowded the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yidougui had served Zhao with great diligence, and tribute crowded the roads.

sentences.zh: 及燕人伐逸豆歸，趙王虎使右將軍白勝、并州刺史王霸自甘松出救之。

translations.literal: When the Yan forces attacked Yidougui, Shi Hu, Prince of Zhao, sent Right General Bai Sheng and Inspector of Bingzhou Wang Ba out from Gansong to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan attacked Yidougui, Shi Hu sent Right General Bai Sheng and the inspector of Bingzhou, Wang Ba, out from Gansong to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 比至，宇文氏已亡，因攻威德城，不克而還；

translations.literal: By the time they arrived the Yuwen clan had already perished; they therefore attacked Weide but could not take it and returned;
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived the Yuwen had already been destroyed; they therefore attacked Weide, failed to take it, and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 慕容彪追擊，破之。

translations.literal: Murong Biao pursued and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Biao pursued and routed them.

sentences.zh: 慕容翰之與宇文氏戰也，為流矢所中，臥病積時不出。

translations.literal: When Murong Han fought the Yuwen, he was struck by a stray arrow and lay ill for a long time without going out.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Han fought the Yuwen he was struck by a stray arrow and lay ill for a long time without going abroad.

sentences.zh: 後漸差，於其家試騁馬。

translations.literal: Later he improved somewhat and tested a galloping horse at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he improved somewhat and tested a galloping horse at his home.

sentences.zh: 或告翰稱病而私飛騎乘，疑欲為變。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Han claimed illness yet privately rode a swift horse, suspecting he intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Han claimed illness yet privately rode a swift horse, raising suspicion that he meant to rebel.

sentences.zh: 燕王皝雖藉翰勇略，然中心終忌之，乃賜翰死。

translations.literal: Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, though he relied on Han's courage and stratagems, inwardly always feared him and therefore ordered Han to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang, though he relied on Han's courage and stratagems, inwardly always feared him and therefore ordered him to die.

sentences.zh: 翰曰：「吾負罪出奔，既而復還，今日死已晚矣。

translations.literal: Han said, "I fled in guilt, then returned; to die today is already late.
translations.idiomatic: Han said, "I fled in guilt and later returned—to die today is already late.

sentences.zh: 然羯賊跨據中原，吾不自量，欲為國家蕩壹區夏。

translations.literal: Yet the Jie bandits hold the Central Plains; I overestimated myself in wishing to sweep one realm for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Jie bandits hold the Central Plains; I overestimated myself in wishing to sweep the realm clean for the state.

sentences.zh: 此志不遂，沒有遺恨，命矣夫！

translations.literal: This ambition was not fulfilled—when I die I have no regret. It is fate!"
translations.idiomatic: That ambition was not fulfilled—when I die I have no regret. It is fate!"

sentences.zh: 」飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: He drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank poison and died.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍遣其大人長孫秩迎婦於燕。

translations.literal: Dai King Shiyijian sent his great chief Changsun Zhi to fetch his bride from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai King Shiyijian sent his great chief Changsun Zhi to fetch his bride from Yan.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，涼州將張瓘敗趙將王擢於三交城。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhang Guan, general of Liangzhou, defeated Zhao general Wang Zhuo at Sanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhang Guan, a general of Liangzhou, defeated the Zhao general Wang Zhuo at Sanjiao.

sentences.zh: 初，趙領軍王朗言於趙王虎曰：「盛冬雪寒，而皇太子使人伐宮材，引於漳水，役者數萬，吁嗟滿道，陛下宜因出遊罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Lang, Director of the Guards of Zhao, said to Shi Hu, Prince of Zhao, "Deep winter and snowy cold—and the crown prince has men felling palace timber and hauling it to the Zhang River; tens of thousands of corvée laborers fill the roads with groans. Your Majesty should take the occasion of an outing tour to halt it."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Lang, director of the guards, said to Shi Hu, "In deep winter's snow and cold the crown prince has men felling palace timber and hauling it to the Zhang River; tens of thousands of laborers fill the roads with groans. Your Majesty should use an outing tour as the occasion to halt it."

sentences.zh: 」虎從之。

translations.literal: Hu complied.
translations.idiomatic: Hu agreed.

sentences.zh: 太子宣怒。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Xuan was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Xuan was furious.

sentences.zh: 會熒惑守房，宣使太史令趙攬言於虎曰：「房為天王，今熒惑守之，其殃不細。

translations.literal: When Mars occupied the House asterism, Xuan had Grand Astrologer Zhao Lan tell Hu, "The House is the asterism of the Son of Heaven; now Mars guards it—the calamity is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Mars occupied the House asterism, Xuan had the grand astrologer Zhao Lan tell Hu, "The House is the asterism of the Son of Heaven; now Mars guards it—the calamity is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 宜以貴臣王姓者當之。

translations.literal: A noble minister surnamed Wang should bear it in his stead."
translations.idiomatic: A noble minister surnamed Wang should bear it in his stead."

sentences.zh: 」虎曰：「誰可者？

translations.literal: Hu said, "Who is suitable?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "Who is suitable?"

sentences.zh: 」攬曰：「無貴於王領軍。

translations.literal: Lan said, "None nobler than Director Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Lan said, "None nobler than Director Wang."

sentences.zh: 」虎意惜朗，使攬更言其次。

translations.literal: Hu cherished Lang and had Lan name the next choice.
translations.idiomatic: Hu cherished Lang and had Lan name the next choice.

sentences.zh: 攬無以對，因曰：「其次唯中書監王波耳。

translations.literal: Lan had no reply and therefore said, "The next is only Director of the Secretariat Wang Bo."
translations.idiomatic: Lan had no reply and therefore said, "The next is only Director of the Secretariat Wang Bo."

sentences.zh: 」虎乃下詔，追罪波前議枯矢事，腰斬之，及其四子，投屍漳水；

translations.literal: Hu then issued an edict, prosecuting Bo on the earlier matter of debating the "withered arrow" and executing him by waist-slicing together with his four sons, casting the corpses into the Zhang River;
translations.idiomatic: Hu then issued an edict, prosecuting Bo on the earlier debate over the "withered arrow," executing him by waist-slicing together with his four sons and casting the corpses into the Zhang River;

sentences.zh: 既而愍其無罪，追贈司空，封其孫為侯。

translations.literal: afterward pitying his innocence he posthumously awarded him Minister of Works and enfeoffed his grandson as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: afterward, pitying his innocence, he posthumously made him Minister of Works and enfeoffed his grandson as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 趙平北將軍尹農攻燕凡城，不克而還。

translations.literal: Yin Nong, Zhao's General Who Pacifies the North, attacked Fancheng of Yan but could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Nong, Zhao's general who pacifies the north, attacked Fancheng of Yan but could not take it and returned.

sentences.zh: 漢太史令韓皓上言：「熒惑守心，乃宗廟不修之譴。

translations.literal: Han Grand Astrologer Han Hao memorialized, "Mars guarding the Heart is Heaven's reproach for neglect of the ancestral temples."
translations.idiomatic: Han Grand Astrologer Han Hao memorialized, "Mars guarding the Heart is Heaven's reproach for neglect of the ancestral temples."

sentences.zh: 」漢主勢命群臣議之。

translations.literal: Han ruler Shi ordered the ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Shi ordered the ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 相國董皎、侍中王嘏以為：「景、武創業，獻、文承基，至親不遠，無宜疏絕。

translations.literal: Chancellor Dong Jiao and Palace Attendant Wang Gu held that "Jing and Wu founded the enterprise; Xian and Wen carried on the foundation—close kin should not be cast off."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Dong Jiao and Palace Attendant Wang Gu held that "Jing and Wu founded the enterprise and Xian and Wen carried on the foundation—close kin should not be cast off."

sentences.zh: 」乃更命祀成始祖、太宗，皆謂之漢。

translations.literal: They therefore renewed sacrifices to Founder and Grand Ancestor, both styled Han.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore renewed sacrifices to the founding ancestor and the grand ancestor, both styled Han.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍庾翼使梁州刺史桓宣擊趙將李羆於丹水，為羆所敗，翼貶宣為建威將軍。

translations.literal: Campaign-west General Yu Yi had Liangzhou Inspector Huan Xuan attack Zhao general Li Pi at Danshui; Xuan was defeated by Pi, and Yi demoted Xuan to General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign-west General Yu Yi had Liangzhou inspector Huan Xuan attack the Zhao general Li Pi at Danshui; Xuan was defeated by Pi, and Yi demoted him to general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 宣慚憤成疾，秋，八月，庚辰，卒。

translations.literal: Xuan, shamed and resentful, fell ill; in autumn, the eighth month, on gengchen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, shamed and resentful, fell ill; in autumn, the eighth month, on gengchen, he died.

sentences.zh: 翼以長子方之為義城太守，代領宣眾；

translations.literal: Yi made his eldest son Fangzhi Administrator of Yicheng to take command of Xuan's troops in his stead;
translations.idiomatic: Yi made his eldest son Fangzhi administrator of Yicheng to take command of Xuan's troops in his stead;

sentences.zh: 又以司馬應誕為襄陽太守，參軍司馬勳為梁州刺史，戍西城。

translations.literal: he also made Sima Yingdan Administrator of Xiangyang, staff officer Sima Xun Inspector of Liangzhou, garrisoning Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: he also made Sima Yingdan administrator of Xiangyang, staff officer Sima Xun inspector of Liangzhou, garrisoning Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 中書令褚裒固辭樞要；

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Chu Pou firmly declined the key post at court;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Chu Pou firmly declined a key post at court;

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁巳，以裒為左將軍、都督兗州、徐州之琅邪諸軍事、兗州刺史，鎮金城。

translations.literal: in the intercalary month, on dingsi, he was made Left General, commander of military affairs in Yanzhou and the Langye region of Xuzhou, and Inspector of Yanzhou, stationed at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: in the intercalary month, on dingsi, he was made left general, commander of military affairs in Yanzhou and the Langye region of Xuzhou, and inspector of Yanzhou, stationed at Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，庾冰、庾翼欲立會稽王昱為嗣；

translations.literal: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was gravely ill; Yu Bing and Yu Yi wished to install Prince Kuaiji of Kuaiji as heir;

sentences.zh: 中書監何充建議立皇子聃，帝從之。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat He Chong proposed installing the imperial son Dan, and the emperor followed him.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，立聃為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on bingchen, Dan was installed as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝崩於式乾殿。

translations.literal: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu the emperor died in Shigan Hall.

sentences.zh: 己亥，何充以遺旨奉太子即位，大赦。

translations.literal: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai He Chong, by the late emperor's testament, installed the crown prince and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 由是冰、翼深恨充。

translations.literal: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.
translations.idiomatic: From this Bing and Yi deeply resented Chong.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后褚氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress of the Chu clan was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 時穆帝方二歲，太后臨朝稱制。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Mu was just two years old; the empress dowager held court and ruled in her own name.

sentences.zh: 何充加中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He Chong was additionally made Director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong was additionally made director of the Secretariat with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs.

sentences.zh: 充自陳既錄尚書，不宜復監中書；

translations.literal: Chong himself stated that having authority to record the Masters of Writing, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Chong himself stated that having authority to record Masters of Writing affairs, he ought not again to oversee the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 許之，復加侍中。

translations.literal: this was granted, and he was additionally made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: this was granted, and he was additionally made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 充以左將軍褚裒，太后之父，宜綜朝政，上疏薦裒參錄尚書；

translations.literal: Chong, considering that Left General Chu Pou was the empress dowager's father and ought to oversee court government, memorialized recommending Pou to assist in recording Masters of Writing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Chong, considering that Left General Chu Pou was the empress dowager's father and ought to oversee court government, memorialized recommending Pou to assist in recording Masters of Writing affairs;

sentences.zh: 乃以裒為侍中、衛將軍、錄尚書事，持節、督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Pou was therefore made Palace Attendant, Defender General, with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs; his credential staff, command, and inspector title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Pou was therefore made palace attendant and defender general with authority to record Masters of Writing affairs; his credential staff, command, and inspector title remained as before.

sentences.zh: 裒以近戚，懼獲譏嫌，上疏固請居籓；

translations.literal: Pou, as a close kinsman, feared censure and memorialized firmly requesting a post on the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Pou, as a close kinsman, feared censure and memorialized firmly requesting a post on the frontier;

sentences.zh: 改授都督徐、兗、青三州、揚州之二郡諸軍事、衛將軍、徐、兗二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: he was reassigned commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces and two Yangzhou commanderies, Defender General and Inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: he was reassigned commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing and two Yangzhou commanderies, defender general and inspector of Xu and Yan, stationed at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏：「裒見太后，在公庭則如臣禮，私覿則嚴父。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized, "When Pou sees the empress dowager, in the public hall he uses the rites of a subject; in private audience he is the stern father."
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing memorialized, "When Pou sees the empress dowager, in the public hall he uses the rites of a subject; in private audience he is the stern father."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: This was approved.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙丑，葬康帝於崇平陵。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yichou, Emperor Kang was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on yichou, Emperor Kang was buried at Chongping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史庾冰有疾；

translations.literal: Yu Bing, Inspector of Jiangzhou, fell ill;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bing, the inspector of Jiangzhou, fell ill;

sentences.zh: 太后征冰輔政，冰辭，十一月，庚辰，卒。

translations.literal: the empress dowager summoned Bing to assist in government; Bing declined; in the eleventh month, on gengchen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: the empress dowager summoned Bing to assist in government; Bing declined; in the eleventh month, on gengchen, he died.

sentences.zh: 庾翼以家國情事，留子方之為建武將軍，戍襄陽。
