translations.literal: Within the city they defended against it; Qiu's host dead and wounded numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders beat them back from inside the walls, and Ma Qiu's army lost tens of thousands killed and wounded.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎復遣其將劉渾等帥步騎二萬會之。

translations.literal: The King of Zhao Hu again sent his generals Liu Hun and others leading twenty thousand foot and horse to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent Liu Hun and other commanders with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to reinforce the siege.

sentences.zh: 郎坦恨言不用，教軍士李嘉潛引趙兵千餘人登城；

translations.literal: Lang Tan resented that his words were not used; he taught the soldier Li Jia secretly to lead more than a thousand Zhao troops onto the wall;
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan, bitter that his counsel had been ignored, induced a trooper named Li Jia to smuggle more than a thousand Zhao soldiers onto the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 璩督諸將力戰，殺二百餘人，趙兵乃退。

translations.literal: Qu supervised the generals in fierce battle, killed more than two hundred men, and the Zhao troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qu rallied the officers in a stiff fight, cut down over two hundred of the enemy, and drove the Zhao climbers back.

sentences.zh: 璩燒其攻具，秋退保大夏。

translations.literal: Qu burned their siege engines; Qiu withdrew and garrisoned Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qu burned the attackers' engines; Ma Qiu pulled back and regrouped at Daxia.

sentences.zh: 虎以中書監石寧為征西將軍，帥並、司州兵二萬餘人為秋等後繼。

translations.literal: Hu appointed Supervising Secretary Shi Ning as General Who Conquers the West, leading more than twenty thousand troops of Bing and Si provinces as rear support for Qiu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu named Chief Secretariat Supervisor Shi Ning western-expedition general and sent him with over twenty thousand men from Bing and Si to follow up on Ma Qiu.

sentences.zh: 張重華將宋秦等帥戶二萬降於趙。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua's generals Song Qin and others led twenty thousand households in surrender to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qin and other officers under Zhang Chonghua defected with twenty thousand registered households.

sentences.zh: 重華以謝艾為使持節、軍師將軍，帥步騎三萬進軍臨河。

translations.literal: Chonghua made Xie Ai Bearer of the Staff, General of the Staff Army, and led thirty thousand foot and horse to advance the army to Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua commissioned Xie Ai as staff-bearing marshal and army strategist and sent him forward to the Lin River with thirty thousand infantry and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 艾乘軺車，戴白窺，鳴鼓而行。

translations.literal: Ai rode a light carriage, wore a white cap, and advanced beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai came in an open light cart, a white kerchief on his head, drums sounding as he marched.

sentences.zh: 秋望見，怒曰：「艾年少書生，冠服如此，輕我也」。

translations.literal: Qiu saw him and angrily said: "Ai is a young scholar; dress like this—he belittles me!"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu caught sight of him and raged: "That stripling clerk in scholar's robes — he's mocking me!"

sentences.zh: 命黑槊龍驤三千人馳擊之，艾左右大擾。

translations.literal: He ordered three thousand Black-Spear Dragon-Chargers to gallop and strike them; on Ai's left and right great disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed three thousand Black-Spear "Dragon Charger" shock troops; Xie Ai's escort fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 或勸艾宜乘馬，艾不從，下車，踞胡床，指麾處分；

translations.literal: Some urged Ai that he ought to mount a horse; Ai did not follow, dismounted the carriage, squatted on a folding camp-chair, and pointed and deployed assignments;
translations.idiomatic: Advisers told him to take a horse; he refused, stepped down, sat on a folding camp chair, and directed the battle by gesture.

sentences.zh: 趙人以為有伏兵，懼不敢進。

translations.literal: The Zhao men thought there were concealed troops; they feared and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao troops took his calm for an ambush and hung back in fear.

sentences.zh: 別將張瑁自間道引兵截趙軍後，趙軍退，艾乘勢進擊，大破之，斬其將杜勳、汲魚，獲首虜一萬三千級，秋單馬奔大夏。

translations.literal: The separate general Zhang Mao by a hidden path led troops to cut off the Zhao army's rear; the Zhao army withdrew, Ai seized the momentum to advance and strike, greatly defeated them, beheaded their generals Du Xun and Ji Yu, captured heads and captives thirteen thousand levels, Qiu alone on horse fled to Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhang Mao had slipped along a back trail to hit the Zhao rear; when they broke, Xie Ai pressed the rout, smashed them utterly, killed the generals Du Xun and Ji Yu, and took thirteen thousand heads and prisoners — Ma Qiu fled alone to Daxia.

sentences.zh: 五月，秋與石寧復帥眾十二萬進屯河南，劉寧、王擢略地晉興、廣武、武街，至於曲柳。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Qiu and Shi Ning again led a host of one hundred twenty thousand, advanced and encamped south of the River; Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo overran Jinxing, Guangwu, Wujie, reaching Qu Liu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ma Qiu and Shi Ning returned with a hundred and twenty thousand men and camped on the south bank of the Yellow River; Liu Ning and Wang Zhuo overran the border posts of Jinxing, Guangwu, and Wujie as far as Qu Liu.

sentences.zh: 張重華使將軍牛旋御之，退守枹罕，姑臧大震。

translations.literal: Zhang Chonghua sent the general Niu Xuan to resist them; he retreated to garrison Fuhan, and Guzang shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua sent Niu Xuan to meet them; Niu Xuan fell back on Fuhan, and the capital Guzang trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 重華欲親出拒之，謝艾固諫。

translations.literal: Chonghua wished personally to go out to resist them; Xie Ai firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua meant to take the field in person; Xie Ai argued him down.

sentences.zh: 別駕從事索遐曰：「君者，一國之鎮，不可輕動」。

translations.literal: Privy Escort Attendant Suo Xia said: "The lord is the buttress of a whole state — he must not move lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Privy secretary Suo Xia said, "You are the pillar of the realm; you cannot expose yourself."

sentences.zh: 乃以艾為使持節、都督征討諸軍事、行衛將軍，遐為軍正將軍，帥步騎二萬拒之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they made Ai Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Punitive Campaign Forces over All Armies, Acting Defender General, and Xia Army Rectifier General; they led twenty thousand foot and horse to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: They gave Xie Ai supreme punitive command with twenty thousand foot and horse, Suo Xia as army rectifier, and sent the pair to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 別將楊康敗劉寧於沙阜，寧退屯金城。

translations.literal: The separate general Yang Kang defeated Liu Ning at Sandy Mound; Ning withdrew and encamped at Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Kang routed Liu Ning on Sandy Hill; Liu Ning pulled back to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 六月，辛酉，大赦。

translations.literal: Sixth month, xinyou day: great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth month's xinyou day the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，林邑復陷日南，殺督護劉雄。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Linyi again took Rinan, killed Superintendent Liu Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Linyi again overran Rinan and killed the protector Liu Xiong.

sentences.zh: 隗文、鄧定等立故國師範長生之子賁為帝而奉之，以妖異惑眾，蜀人多歸之。

translations.literal: Wei Wen, Deng Ding, and others set up Fan the son of the former state teacher Fan Changsheng as emperor and served him, using demonic wonders to bewitch the masses; many in Shu submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wen and Deng Ding enthroned the son of the Daoist master Fan Changsheng and worked occult wonders on the crowd until much of Shu fell in behind them.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎復遣征西將軍孫伏都、將軍劉渾帥步騎二萬會麻秋軍，長驅濟河，擊張重華，遂城長最。

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao again sent General Who Conquers the West Sun Fudu and General Liu Hun leading twenty thousand foot and horse to join Ma Qiu's army; they drove straight across the river, struck Zhang Chonghua, and forthwith walled Changzui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu again sent Sun Fudu and Liu Hun with twenty thousand men to join Ma Qiu, crossed the Yellow River in a long drive, hammered Zhang Chonghua, and threw up a fortress at Changzui.

sentences.zh: 謝艾建牙誓眾，有風吹旌旗東南指，索遐曰：「風為號令，今旌旗指敵，天所贊也。

translations.literal: Xie Ai raised the battle standard and swore the host; there was wind that blew the flags southeast; Suo Xia said: "Wind is a signal; now the banners point at the foe — Heaven approves.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai assembled the troops under the war banners; a wind snapped the standards toward the southeast. Suo Xia cried, "Wind is Heaven's command — see how the flags turn on the enemy!

sentences.zh: 」艾軍於神鳥，王擢與艾前鋒戰，敗走，還河南。

translations.literal: " Ai encamped at Divine Bird; Wang Zhuo fought with Ai's vanguard, was defeated and fled, returned to south of the River.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai pitched at Divine Bird; Wang Zhuo's van was beaten and fled back across the river.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，艾進擊秋，大破之，秋遁歸金城。

translations.literal: Eighth month, wuwu day: Ai advanced and struck Qiu, greatly defeated him; Qiu fled back to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth month's wuwu day Xie Ai smashed Ma Qiu again; Ma Qiu ran for Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 虎聞之，歎曰：「吾以偏師定九州，今以九州之力困於枹罕。

translations.literal: Hu heard of it and sighed: "I with a detached division settled the Nine Provinces; now with the strength of the Nine Provinces I am trapped at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Hu heard, he groaned, "Once a single column of mine took the empire — now all Zhao strains against one Fuhan!

sentences.zh: 彼有人焉，未可圖也！

translations.literal: There are capable men over there — they cannot yet be taken!
translations.idiomatic: They have talent in that corner. The place is not to be had yet.

sentences.zh: 」艾還，討叛虜斯骨真等萬餘落，皆破平之。

translations.literal: " Ai returned and punished the rebellious barbarians Si Guzhen and others, more than ten thousand lodges, all broken and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Xie Ai broke more than ten thousand rebel tribes under Si Guzhen and the like.

sentences.zh: 趙王虎據十州之地，聚斂金帛，及外國所獻珍異，府庫財物，不可勝紀；

translations.literal: King Hu of Zhao held the territory of ten provinces, amassed gold and silks, and the rare curios presented by foreign states; treasuries and goods beyond reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu held ten provinces, piled tax gold and foreign tribute until the vaults could not be counted;

sentences.zh: 猶自以為不足，悉發前代陵墓，取其金寶。

translations.literal: yet he still thought it insufficient, and completely opened the tombs of former dynasties, taking their gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: yet called it too little and plundered the royal graves of earlier ages for their treasure.

sentences.zh: 沙門吳進言於虎曰：「胡運將衰，晉當復興，宜苦役晉人以厭其氣。

translations.literal: The monk Wu Jin spoke to Hu saying: "Hu fortune is about to decline; Jin is about to revive — you ought to work the Jin people hard to suppress their qi.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wu Jin told him, "The barbarian fate wanes; the Jin line will rise again — grind the Han people with forced labor to crush their vital force.

sentences.zh: 」虎使尚書張群發近郡男女十六萬人，車十萬乘，運士築華林苑及長牆於鄴北，廣袤數十里。

translations.literal: " Hu had Secretariat Director Zhang Qun mobilize one hundred sixty thousand men and women of nearby commanderies, one hundred thousand carts, to transport earth and build the Hualin Park and Long Wall north of Ye, several tens of li in breadth and length.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had Zhang Qun draft a hundred and sixty thousand men and women from the neighboring districts, a hundred thousand wagons of earth, and raise the Hualin Park and the long rampart north of Ye across dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 申鐘、石璞、趙攬等上疏陳天文錯亂，百姓凋弊。

translations.literal: Shen Zhong, Shi Pu, Zhao Lan, and others submitted memorials stating that celestial signs were in disorder and the common people were withered in decline.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhong, Shi Pu, Zhao Lan, and others warned that the stars were awry and the people ruined.

sentences.zh: 虎大怒曰：「使苑牆朝成，吾夕沒無恨矣。

translations.literal: Hu roared in great anger: "Let the park wall stand by morning — I will die at evening without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu thundered, "If the park wall stands by dawn, I will die at dusk content.

sentences.zh: 」促張群使然燭夜作；

translations.literal: " He hurried Zhang Qun to make lamps burn through the night for work;
translations.idiomatic: He drove Zhang Qun to work the laborers by torchlight through the night;

sentences.zh: 暴風大雨，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Violent wind and great rain; the dead numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: a storm broke; tens of thousands perished.

sentences.zh: 郡國前後送蒼麟十六，白鹿七，虎命司虞張曷柱調之以駕芝蓋，大朝會列於殿庭。

translations.literal: Commanderies before and after sent sixteen blue unicorns and seven white deer; Hu ordered Herds Intendant Zhang Hezhu to train them to draw fungus canopy carriages, at the great court assembly arrayed in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Districts sent sixteen blue deer and seven white stags; Shi Hu had the herds intendant break them to the rein for fungus-canopied state coaches and parade them in the forecourt at a grand audience.

sentences.zh: 九月，命太子宣出祈福於山川，因行遊獵。

translations.literal: Ninth month: ordered the Heir Apparent Xuan to go out to pray for blessings at mountains and rivers, and thereby to roam and hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he sent the crown prince Shi Xuan to pray at the rivers and mountains — and to hunt on the way.

sentences.zh: 宣乘大輅，羽葆華蓋，建天子旌旗，十有六軍戎卒十八萬，出自金明門。

translations.literal: Xuan rode the great carriage, feather canopy and flowered parasol, set up Son-of-Heaven banners and flags, sixteen armies, one hundred eighty thousand field troops, and went out through the Golden Bright Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rolled out in the imperial chariot with feathered canopy and flowered parasol, imperial banners flying, sixteen corps and a hundred and eighty thousand men behind him through the Golden Bright Gate.

sentences.zh: 虎從其後宮升陵霄觀望之，笑曰：「我家父子如是，自非天崩地陷，當復何愁！

translations.literal: Hu from his rear palace ascended Spirit-Cloud Terrace to gaze on them and laughed: "Father and son of my house like this — unless Heaven and Earth collapse, what worry remains!
translations.idiomatic: From the Spirit-Cloud Pavilion Shi Hu watched the host and laughed: "With father and son like this, unless heaven falls and earth cracks, what is left to fear?

sentences.zh: 但抱子弄孫，日為樂耳。

translations.literal: Only to hold a son and dandle a grandson, day by day making joy.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing but to dandle grandchildren and take one's ease day by day.

sentences.zh: 宣所捨，輒列人為長圍，四面各百里，驅禽獸，至暮皆集其所，使文武跪立，重行圍守，炬火如晝，命勁騎百餘馳射其中，宣與姬妾乘輦臨觀，獸盡而止。

translations.literal: Wherever Xuan halted, he immediately arrayed men in a long enclosure, each side a hundred li, drove birds and beasts, and by evening all gathered at his place; he made civil and military kneel and stand, double-ranked enclosure guard, torch-fires like midday, ordered powerful cavalry more than a hundred to gallop and shoot within it; Xuan with concubines rode the palanquin to overlook; when beasts were exhausted then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Xuan camped he threw a hundred-li cordon on every side, drove game inward until dusk, made officials and soldiers kneel in ranks with torches bright as noonday, and sent a hundred picked horsemen to ride the ring shooting down the animals while he and his women watched from a litter until nothing stirred.

sentences.zh: 或獸有迸逸，當圍守者，有爵則奪馬，步驅一日，無爵則鞭之一百。

translations.literal: Or if a beast burst out and escaped, for those who should guard the enclosure, if they had noble rank then the horse was taken away, they walked and drove for one day; if no noble rank then one hundred lashes.
translations.idiomatic: Any beast that broke the ring cost a noble his mount and a day's march on foot; common soldiers earned a hundred strokes of the whip.

sentences.zh: 士卒饑凍死者萬有餘人，所過三州十五郡，資儲皆無孑遺。

translations.literal: Soldiers who starved and froze to death were more than ten thousand; the three provinces and fifteen commanderies they passed through, supplies and stores all without a single remnant.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand soldiers died of hunger and cold; three provinces and fifteen commanderies were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 虎覆命秦公韜繼出，自并州至於秦、雍，亦如之。

translations.literal: Hu again ordered Duke of Qin Tao to follow and go out, from Bing Province reaching Qin and Yong — likewise so.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu ordered his son Shi Tao, Duke of Qin, on the same sort of expedition from Bing province through Qin and Yong.

sentences.zh: 宣怒其與己鈞敵，愈嫉之。

translations.literal: Xuan was angry that he matched himself; the more he envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hated the equal display and nursed deeper spite.

sentences.zh: 宦者趙生得幸於宣，無寵於韜，微勸宣除之，於是始有殺韜之謀矣。

translations.literal: The eunuch Zhao Sheng gained favor with Xuan, had no favor with Tao; he subtly urged Xuan to remove him — then there began to be a plot to kill Tao.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Zhao Sheng, favored by Xuan but not by Tao, whispered that Tao should be removed — and the murder plot began.

sentences.zh: 趙麻秋又襲張重華將張瑁，敗之，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Zhao Ma Qiu again raided Zhang Chonghua's officer Zhang Mao, defeated him, beheaded more than three thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu raided Zhang Mao, routed him, and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 枹罕護軍李逵帥眾七千降於趙，自河以南氐、羌皆附於趙。

translations.literal: Fuhan Garrison Commander Li Kui led a host of seven thousand in surrender to Zhao; south of the river Di and Qiang all attached to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui, garrison commander of Fuhan, surrendered seven thousand men to Zhao; Di and Qiang south of the river went over in mass.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙丑，遣侍御史俞歸至涼州，授張重華侍中、大都督、督隴右、關中諸軍事、大將軍、涼州刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, yichou day: sent Attendant Imperial Censor Yu Gui to Liangzhou, invested Zhang Chonghua as Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, Commander of Longyou and Guanzhong Military Affairs, Great General, Governor of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the court dispatched the censor Yu Gui to Liangzhou to invest Zhang Chonghua as palace attendant, supreme commander of Longyou and the Guanzhong armies, general-in-chief, Liangzhou governor, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 歸至姑臧，重華欲稱涼王，未肯受詔，使所親沈猛私謂歸曰：「主公弈世為晉忠臣，今曾不如鮮卑，何也？

translations.literal: Gui reached Guzang; Chonghua wished to style himself King of Liang and was not willing to receive the edict; he sent his intimate Shen Meng privately to tell Gui: "My lord for generations has been a loyal minister of Jin; now he is not even equal to the Xianbei — why?
translations.idiomatic: At Guzang, Zhang Chonghua wanted the title King of Liang and hesitated to accept the patent; his confidant Shen Meng told Yu Gui privately, "Our master has been Jin's loyal vassal for generations — how is he now ranked below the Xianbei?

sentences.zh: 朝廷封慕容皝為燕王，而主公才為大將軍，何以褒勸忠賢乎！

translations.literal: The court enfeoffed Murong Huang as King of Yan, while my lord is only a great general — how reward and encourage loyal worthies!
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang was made King of Yan while our lord stops at general-in-chief — is that how you honor faithful service!

sentences.zh: 明台宜移河右，共勸州主為涼王。

translations.literal: The bright terrace ought to move west of the river; together urge the provincial lord as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Move the court west and jointly urge the Prince of Liang upon him.

sentences.zh: 人臣出使，苟利社稷，專之可也。

translations.literal: A minister on mission, if it profits the state-altar, may act on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy who serves the realm may act on his own when the need is clear.

sentences.zh: 」歸曰：「吾子失言！

translations.literal: " Gui said: "My son, you speak wrongly!
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gui replied, "Young man, that is disloyal talk."

sentences.zh: 昔三代之王也，爵之貴者莫若上公；

translations.literal: In antiquity the kings of the Three Dynasties — of nobility in enfeoffment none was higher than Duke Supporter;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Three Dynasties the highest enfeoffment was Duke of the First Rank;

sentences.zh: 及周之衰，吳、楚始僭號稱王，而諸侯亦不之非，蓋以蠻夷畜之也；

translations.literal: when Zhou declined, Wu and Chu first usurped the title and called themselves kings, while the feudal lords also did not condemn them — because they stored them as barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: when Zhou weakened Wu and Chu first styled themselves kings without censure from the other lords, because they were treated as outer barbarians.

sentences.zh: 借使齊、魯稱王，諸侯豈不四面攻之乎！

translations.literal: If Qi and Lu were to call themselves kings, would the feudal lords not attack from all four sides!
translations.idiomatic: Had Qi or Lu claimed kingship, the other states would have torn them apart from every side.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖封韓、彭為王，尋皆誅滅，蓋權時之宜，非厚之也。

translations.literal: Han Gaozu enfeoffed Han and Peng as kings, but soon both were exterminated and extinguished — because it was expedient for the moment, not to honor them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu made Han Xin and Peng Yue kings and soon destroyed them — a moment's tactic, not a lasting honor.

sentences.zh: 聖上以貴公忠賢，故爵以上公，任以方伯，寵榮極矣，豈鮮卑夷狄所可比哉！

translations.literal: The Sage-Emperor because you, my lord, are loyal and worthy therefore enfeoffs with Duke Supporter, entrusts with regional command, favor and glory at the extreme — how can he be compared to Xianbei barbarian aliens!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has given your master the highest noble rank and full regional command — a peak of honor not to be compared with frontier barbarians!

sentences.zh: 且吾聞之，功有大小，賞有重輕。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard: merit has size, reward has weight and lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Merit has its measure, and reward its scale.

sentences.zh: 今貴公始繼世而為王，若帥河右之眾，東平胡、羯，修復陵廟，迎天子返洛陽，將何以加之乎？

translations.literal: Now if you, my lord, have just succeeded and become king, if you lead the hosts west of the river to level the Hu and Jie eastward, restore the imperial tombs, and welcome the Son of Heaven back to Luoyang — by what will they be increased?
translations.idiomatic: If your lord, newly come to his post, led the armies of the west to crush the barbarians eastward, rebuilt the imperial shrines, and escorted the emperor home to Luoyang — what title would then be left to add?

sentences.zh: 」重華乃止。

translations.literal: " Chonghua then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 武都氐王楊初遣使來稱籓；

translations.literal: Di King Yang Chu of Wudu sent envoys to declare himself vassal;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chu, Di king of Wudu, sent envoys offering allegiance;

sentences.zh: 詔以初為使持節、征南將軍、雍州刺史、仇池公。

translations.literal: an edict made Chu Bearer of the Staff, General Who Conquers the South, Governor of Yongzhou, Duke of Chou.
translations.idiomatic: The court named him staff-bearer, southern-expedition general, Yongzhou governor, and Duke of Chou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，振威護軍蕭敬文殺征虜將軍楊謙，攻涪城，陷之，自稱益州牧，遂取巴西，通於漢中。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Zhenwei Garrison Commander Xiao Jingwen killed Expeditioner-General Yang Qian, attacked Fucheng, took it, styled himself Governor of Yizhou, then seized Brazil, communicated with Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xiao Jingwen, garrison commander of Zhenwei, killed Yang Qian, stormed Fucheng, declared himself Yizhou governor, overran Brazil, and opened contact with Hanzhong.

translations.idiomatic: category: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
